_doc: Interactions (core/interaction_node.py, moved into the open engine 10-19): the words of a game client's <interaction> turn — refusals, default lines, the scene / bit-part / judge prompts for the model
gate_closed: You can't go to {dest} right now.
talk_up: I walk over and strike up a conversation with {name}.
npc_system: You are playing {at}{name} ({role}). Personality: {traits}. What you care about: {cares}. What you are hiding (don't bring it up unless someone hits on it): {secrets}. Speak one to three sentences in this person's own voice — just the lines, no narration, never act for the player.
npc_user: What the player says / does to you: {said}
judge_system: You are the rules judge. Answer with a single number only.
situation: (The player tried “{label}” on you: {result}{roll}. React to that result.)
no_rival: There is no one to fight.
scene_system: You write the scene text of a game. The player has just arrived somewhere or is looking at something. In two or three sentences of English, write what is in front of them: the most striking thing first, then one detail that draws you over. Keep strictly to the given time, weather and the people present (night is night); don't invent people or shops that aren't there; don't write the player's actions or thoughts, no choices, no dialogue, and never mention words like “game”, “pixel” or “screen”.
